Add a line of text from a data column to every tile

Source: R/ggPSE_text.R
ggPSE_text.Rd

Adds one extra text line per element to a plot created with [ggPSE()] (or any function built on it), taking the text from a column of your data. It replaces the usual workaround of merging the element positions into your data and placing a geom_text() by hand. Call it several times to stack more lines, for example a classification at the "center" and a value at the "bottom".

Usage

ggPSE_text(
  plot = NULL,
  data,
  text_col,
  symbol_col = "symbol",
  position = c("bottom", "top", "center"),
  position_nudge = 0,
  size = 2.5,
  fontface = "plain",
  color = "grey15",
  lineheight = 0.9
)

Arguments

plot

A plot created with [ggPSE()]. If NULL, a blank periodic table is used.

data

A data frame with the element symbols and the text column.

text_col

Character. Column in data with the text to draw. It is converted with as.character(), so format numbers beforehand (e.g. with sprintf()).

symbol_col

Character. Column in data with the element symbols. Default "symbol".

position

Where in the tile the text is anchored: "bottom" (default), "top" or "center".

position_nudge

Numeric. Vertical shift in tile units (positive = up) added to position, to fine-tune the placement. A tile is 0.92 high. Default 0. (Unlike ggplot2::position_nudge() this is a single vertical value.)

size

Numeric. Text size in ggplot2 text units (mm). Default 2.5.

fontface

Character. "plain" (default), "bold", "italic" or "bold.italic".

color

Either a single colour (default "grey15") or the name of a column in data that holds one colour per element.

lineheight

Numeric. Line spacing for multi-line text. Default 0.9.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The text is anchored at the chosen edge of the tile and grows into the tile, so multi-line text ("\n") stays inside it. Elements that are not in data, or whose text is NA or empty, get no text. Elements in data that are not part of the plot (e.g. outside a periods subset) are ignored.

Note

[ggPSE_donut()] removes every text layer from the plot it receives. Call ggPSE_text() after the donut.

Examples

data(ggpse_elements)
d <- data.frame(
  symbol = c("Li", "Na", "K", "Fe", "Cu"),
  E      = c(-3.04, -2.71, -2.92, -0.41, 0.34),
  eq     = c("Li\u207a+e\u207b\u2192Li", "Na\u207a+e\u207b\u2192Na",
             "K\u207a+e\u207b\u2192K", "Fe\u00b2\u207a+2e\u207b\u2192Fe",
             "Cu\u00b2\u207a+2e\u207b\u2192Cu")
)
d$E_label <- sprintf("%+.2f", d$E)

p <- ggPSE(d, value_col = "E", label_value = FALSE, label_na = FALSE,
           symbol_position = "center", periods = c(1, 4),
           lanthanides = FALSE, actinides = FALSE)
p <- ggPSE_text(p, d, "E_label", position = "top", fontface = "bold")
ggPSE_text(p, d, "eq", position = "bottom", size = 2)
